Rivers of the North

A field report on braided channels and the sediment they carry.

Overview

At a glance

Length: 1,240 km

Basin: 84,000 km²

Mean flow: 610 m³/s

Source: glacial melt in the eastern highlands, fed by seasonal snowpack.

The northern river systems braid across wide gravel plains, splitting and rejoining around shifting bars. Sediment transport

The blue block to the left is a left-floated figure; this paragraph wraps around its right side. Suspended load dominates in spring, when meltwater lifts fine silt; bedload creeps along the channel floor as the discharge falls through summer. The d50 grain size drops downstream as the current loses competence.
